what: what a precompiled script image saves on a WHOLE page load, not on one stage

supersedes.why_stale: it was recorded before four changes to the load path: two loader optimisations (3a59436, 59d0339), the source hash (4afa905) and the operand bound table (e67a4fa). Its 53% understated the current saving by nineteen points.

tool: ctcompile/tools/ctpageload, run from ctbrowser/examples/pages so the page's <script src> resolves
page: p5-basic.html - three classic scripts: an inline flag, the p5 bundle, and the sketch
findings: SEVENTY-TWO PERCENT OF THIS PAGE'S LOAD WAS COMPILING ITS JAVASCRIPT. 66.80 ms becomes 18.97 ms. What remains is HTML parsing, CSS, style, layout and the image load itself - the work Principle 6 says stays at run time.

THE SOURCE HASH WAS 3.9 ms OF IT, and nobody had noticed it was on the page path. Measured as an interleaved A/B of two binaries built from this tree differing only in image_source_hash: 23.7 ms from image with byte-at-a-time FNV-1a against 19.8 ms with XXH64, six runs each, alternating. That agrees within 0.1 ms with the hash measured on its own (4.16 ms against 0.181 ms for p5's 4.5 MB), which is the only reason to believe either number.

THE 'FROM SOURCE' ARM ALSO MOVED, 72.59 ms to 65.38, and NO COMMIT EXPLAINS IT - nothing on that path changed. It is cross-session variance on a shared VM, and it is why the saving above is attributed by an A/B of two builds rather than by subtracting this file's previous numbers from these.

A MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN FROM A STALE BINARY AND NEARLY RECORDED, and the cause recorded here at first was WRONG. The first reading after a full remote build reported 23.9 ms for a tree that hashes in 0.181; this file blamed rsync -az preserving mtimes. It is not that. ctpageload was EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL, so `cmake --build` never built it AT ALL - the binary in the build tree was the PREVIOUS SESSION'S, which is why its number matched the A/B's old arm to the hundredth of a millisecond. Proven by touching one engine .cpp, running a full default build, and watching the executable's mtime not move. This tree had already been caught by the same mechanism twice, both written up (docs/history/computed-goto.md, docs/performance.md), both ending in an instruction to check the binary - which then failed a third time. It is a build edge now: ctcompile/tools/CMakeLists.txt has a `ctcompile-tools ALL` aggregate, the idiom ctbrowser-tests already used, and the executables are verified to relink on a plain `cmake --build`.
THE MEASUREMENT PROVES THE PATH WAS TAKEN rather than assuming it: the tool exits non-zero unless browser::scripts_compiled_from_source() is 0 after the image run.

A TOOL MUST NOT REPRODUCE THE BROWSER'S CONCATENATION. p5-basic.html has THREE classic scripts, not the one-bundle-plus-sketch shape the first version assumed; a packager that guesses builds an image whose hash never matches, which presents as 'no saving' rather than as a bug. browser::script_source() exists for this and is the API a packager uses.
THE IMAGE IS 1.6x THE SOURCE for this page and the page still loads more than three times faster. Size is not the figure of merit; the parse is.

THE IMAGE LOST 19,028 BYTES TO A FIELD THAT WAS ALWAYS EMPTY. function_proto::nested was serialized as a per-function count of zero; dropping it is exactly 4757 x 4 bytes here, and 128 KB on babylon. The format version went 1 to 2 for it, because unlike the source-hash change this one really did move the layout.
